resources.p_text.a_wedding_video_that_si: A wedding video that sits in a folder is a memory that fades. A wedding video that gets watched — even 30 seconds at a time, once a year — stays alive. Plan for at least 3 specific uses before the wedding. If you don't plan, the video will sit in a folder.
resources.p_text.ai_video_tools_have_mad: AI video tools have made it possible to create wedding films in ways that weren't realistic 3 years ago. But the marketing is often 5 years ahead of the reality. Here's what AI wedding videos actually do well, where they fall short, and when to use them.
resources.p_text.ai_wedding_video_is_a_9: AI wedding video is a 9/10 solution for the 80% of couples who didn't have (or couldn't afford) a real videographer. It's a 6/10 solution for the 20% who had one but want to fix specific issues. If you can afford a real videographer for the day, do that — and use AI for the things traditional videography doesn't solve (restoration, multilingual, style transfer).
resources.p_text.already_have_raw_footag: Already have raw footage and want it edited professionally?
resources.p_text.already_have_raw_weddin: Already have raw wedding footage and want a professional edit?
resources.p_text.be_honest_with_yourself: Be honest with yourself. If you'll only watch a 3-minute film, don't pay for a 6-hour documentary.
resources.p_text.before_shopping_for_vid: Before shopping for videographers, get clear on the deliverable. Most couples don't, and end up disappointed because their expectations were someone else's. The four most common styles:
resources.p_text.five_in_depth_guides_to: Five in-depth guides to help you make better decisions about your wedding video — from choosing a videographer to restoring old footage, with honest talk about pricing, AI, and what actually works.
resources.p_text.for_a_wedding_with_a_no: For a wedding with a normal guest count and a normal budget: $2,500-$4,000 gets you a great wedding video. Below $1,500, you sacrifice post-production quality. Above $8,000, you're paying for things you don't need. Spend the difference on something you'll see every day (the wedding video) rather than something you'll see once (the chair covers).
resources.p_text.get_the_in_between_mome: Get the in-between moments. AI can't capture the look on your grandmother's face when you walk down the aisle. The candid tears during the father-daughter dance. The unexpected toast. These are the moments that matter most, and they only exist if someone was there with a camera.
resources.p_text.have_old_wedding_tapes_: Have old wedding tapes that need restoration?
resources.p_text.have_photos_but_no_vide: Have photos but no video? See what AI can do.
resources.p_text.if_the_tape_plays_at_al: If the tape plays at all → digitize + AI restore ($200-$500). If the tape has damage → professional service with physical cleaning (extra $50-$100). If the tape is unplayable → call a data recovery lab before giving up, but be prepared for the worst. Either way, do it now — not in 5 years.
resources.p_text.ignore_wedding_videogra: Ignore wedding videographer branding ("cinematic", "luxury", "artistic") — those words mean nothing. Watch 3 full wedding films, not highlight reels. Highlight reels are the best 3 minutes of an 8-hour shoot. The full film shows you what you'll actually get.
resources.p_text.match_a_4k_cinematic_sh: Match a 4K cinematic shoot at $500. The current state of the art can do amazing things, but it can't replace a $5,000-$10,000 cinematic production with a team of videographers. The difference shows in shot composition, lighting decisions in real time, and creative problem-solving on the day.
resources.p_text.most_couples_get_their_: Most couples get their wedding video, watch it once on the couch with a glass of wine, save it to a hard drive, and never open it again. Here's how to actually use it.
resources.p_text.play_it_once_and_digiti: play it once and digitize it . The magnetic signal on VHS and 8mm is degrading every year. Five more years of sitting in a box can mean the difference between "slightly faded" and "unplayable."
resources.p_text.reconstruct_someone_who: Reconstruct someone who passed. AI can activate a still photo (subtle movement, blink, smile), and it can use audio recordings to reconstruct a voice. But the results are stylized, not realistic. Don't let anyone sell you "we'll bring grandma back" — what we do is honor her memory with a tasteful, respectful activation. The expectations gap is where families get hurt.
resources.p_text.red_flags.03707568: Red flags: "We'll restore your footage for $50" is almost always just digitization, no AI. "Unlimited revisions" usually means they did nothing the first time. "We use AI" without specifying which tool usually means they're using a consumer app.
resources.p_text.replace_a_real_videogra: Replace a real videographer at the wedding. AI works with footage that exists. If your cousin "got some shots on their phone" — that's 4 minutes of shaky vertical video. AI can't manufacture the footage that wasn't shot. The most common disappointment: couples hoping AI can fix the fact that they didn't hire a videographer. It can't add a missing ceremony.
resources.p_text.restore_degraded_footag: Restore degraded footage. VHS, 8mm, 16mm — all formats that were essentially write-offs 5 years ago are now recoverable. AI can upscale 480p VHS to look like 1080p, color-correct for faded film, and denoise grainy audio. We restored a 1987 wedding that the family thought was gone forever.
resources.p_text.slow_motion_from_standa: Slow motion from standard footage. Your videographer shot at 30fps? AI can interpolate to 120fps or 240fps. The result is buttery smooth slow motion that wasn't in the original footage.
resources.p_text.style_transfer.51006852: Style transfer. Turn your real wedding video into Studio Ghibli, Pixar 3D, anime, watercolor, or comic book style. The output is novel and shareable, not just decorative.
resources.p_text.the_good_news_most_old_: The good news: most old wedding footage is more recoverable than people think. We've restored tapes from 1962, 1987, and 1995 that the family had given up on. Here's a quick guide by format:
resources.p_text.the_line_items_that_go_: The line items that go into a wedding video:
resources.p_text.the_wrong_videographer_: The wrong videographer costs you $3,000-$8,000 and the only memories of a day you can never re-do. The right one is the difference between a video you watch once and a film you watch every anniversary. Here's how to pick.
resources.p_text.translation_and_voiceov: Translation and voiceover. 20+ languages with both subtitles and AI voiceover that mimics the original speaker's accent. For international families, this is genuinely useful.
resources.p_text.turn_still_photos_into_: Turn still photos into a moving film. This is the biggest one. If you have 30-100 photos from a wedding where you didn't hire a videographer, modern AI can create a 2-5 minute film that looks like a real wedding video. Not a slideshow — an actual film with camera movements, transitions, and music synced to beats. We've shipped 100+ of these. The reaction is consistently "I forgot we didn't have a videographer."
resources.p_text.want_shareable_clips_fo: Want shareable clips for your group chat and social media?
resources.p_text.watch_3_full_wedding_fi: Watch 3 full wedding films. If the audio is clear, the camera is steady, and the story flows — book them. If any of those three are off, keep looking. Editing skill, not gear, is what separates a $1,500 video from a $5,000 one.
resources.p_text.wedding_video_prices_ra: Wedding video prices range from $500 to $15,000 for the same event. Here's the honest breakdown of what drives the cost, what you can skip, and where the line is between "fair" and "overpriced."
resources.p_text.whether_you_have_raw_fo: Whether you have raw footage, old tapes, or just a collection of photos, we'll help you figure out the right approach. Free quote, 24-hour response, no commitment.
resources.p_text.your_parents_wedding_vi: Your parents' wedding video is 30 years old and degrading. The colors are fading, the audio is muffled, and parts of the tape are unplayable. Here's what's actually recoverable, what isn't, and how to get it done right.
